messages:
Alex: quick sync — after enabling paged KV on canary we saw allocation stalls under small-req bursts. logging + flamegraph attached in thread below.
Maya: saw that too. fragmentation spike on the slab allocator right?
Shaun: yes, the block-table growth policy is allocating many tiny blocks instead of coalescing. leads to >30% wasted space and some OOM-ish behaviour under sustained 60qps bursts.
Priya: concrete repro? I can run a deterministic load with fixed seq-len to reproduce.
Alex: repro script: ```python run_load.py --model redwood-v1-small --seq 2048 --qps 60 --paged-kv on```
Alex: profile (condensed):
```
GPU memcpy H2D: 18.2%
KV page population (host->device): 28.6%
cudaStreamSynchronize: 15.1%
Attention kernel (FlashA v2): 22.8%
Other: 15.3%
```
Maya: interesting — KV page population is dominant. that suggests allocation churn + memcpy cost, not the attention compute.
Shaun: my notes: current allocator does per-page 4KB sub-alloc; block-table entries are one-per-suballoc. When we have many short contexts we end up with high block-table density, which increases lookup cost in paged-attn path.
Priya: proposed mitigation: switch allocator to slab growth by power-of-two (4KB -> 32KB -> 128KB) and maintain a small free-list for exact-size returns. That should reduce #block-table entries and amortize memcpy.
Alex: also look at backpressure: when mempool is low we still try to schedule large batches. batching heuristics should factor in current free-page count and prefer smaller micro-batches until compaction completes.
Shaun: noted. patch idea: when free_pages < threshold, set max_batch_tokens = min( max_batch_tokens, 0.5 * default ) and disable speculative prefetch for non-active sessions.
Maya: another angle — kernel selection is picking FlashAttn-variant B which expects contiguous KV and gives worse perf if we do many page-boundary accesses. Maybe fall back to fused-attn that tolerates sparse KV for paged mode.
Priya: agree. we can add a cheap metric: pct_unaligned_kv_access = kv_page_crossings / total_kv_accesses. if > 12% prefer fused-attn.
perf-bot: perf regressions summary: canary 2026-11-02 -> +18% p99 latency, +14% token cost. Root cause: allocator fragmentation + memcpy overhead.
Alex: plan for next week: 1) implement slab growth allocator (shaun) 2) batching heuristic change + threshold (maya) 3) kernel selection fallback based on unaligned metric (priya) 4) perf test harness run and baseline before merge (alex).
Shaun: I'll try a prototype today and push a perf patch. expect a small perf dip during compaction but large win long-run.
Maya: I'll add a short-circuit to the batching policy so we can toggle via runtime flag. :thumbsup:
Priya: I'll instrument kv accesses to emit page_crossing counts in trace. will post results.
infra-bot: deploy-canary started for paged-kv-alloc-proto -> canary/slot-7
Alex: thanks everyone. keep replies short here — if you hit repro post logs and the exact `nvprof` snippet.
Maya: uploaded flamegraphs to /artifacts/paged-kv/1768504321/ — look for the memcpy hotspot.
Shaun: quick note: compaction must be cooperative with request handling — do not stall the main inference loop. I'll implement incremental compaction in 8ms quanta.
Priya: incremental compaction sounds good. also we should add unit tests covering block-table eviction order so we avoid regression in the eviction heuristics.
Alex: perfect. will track in PR checklist.
